title: LatentFlow: Discovering Latent Continuous Dynamics across Channels for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: A central difficulty in multivariate time-series anomaly detection is representing intricate dependencies that change over time across variables.

gap.claim: Existing discrete-time approaches face a granularity dilemma and may be biased toward self-dependencies, overlooking subtle cross-channel deviations.

contributions.claim: LatentFlow treats channel dependency evolution as a latent continuous dynamic process.
The framework models channel dependency evolution with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process to capture smooth dependency shifts while maintaining robustness against structural noise.
A Dependency Decoupling Strategy separates and rebalances self-channel and cross-channel patterns.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe LatentFlow as a novel framework for modeling channel dependency evolution as a latent continuous dynamic process.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.
The authors report that the experiments validate the effectiveness of modeling continuous dynamics of dependency evolution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multivariate time series anomaly detection requires modeling complex, evolving dependencies among variables.
Existing methods model channel dependencies in discrete time using window-wise or point-wise approaches.
These approaches trade off sensitivity to transient changes against continuity and noise robustness, while self-dependency bias can obscure cross-channel anomalies.
LatentFlow introduces continuous latent dependency dynamics using an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and decouples self- and cross-channel patterns.
Experiments on multiple real-world datasets are reported to show state-of-the-art performance.
